A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReFeR and retain the same peer-review-inspired framework and several benchmarks. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original NLG evaluation, ablation, Mistral-7B fine-tuning and reasoning results, including Tables 1–10 and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V2 reports original text and multimodal evaluation, reasoning, fine-tuning and framework-analysis results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V2 removes v1's optional critic module and its re-evaluation and weighting pathways. Appendix K explicitly adopts scores-only peer-to-chair communication instead of analyses plus scores; the GSM8k chair prompt likewise changes from reviewing solutions to receiving final answers. These substantially revise the supported information flow, although v2's equations still show comment-score pairs. Turbo/Lite largely name the n=20/n=1 settings already tested in v1.

E1.justification: V2 retains SummEval, TopicalChat, GSM8k and CSQA, adds ICQD caption evaluation and AGIQA image-generation evaluation, and adds AQuA multiple-choice algebra and BBH-DU date reasoning. StrategyQA is removed. Multimodal evaluation, only proposed as future work in v1 Appendix C, is now actually tested.

E2.justification: The reasoning comparison replaces ReConCile and GPT-4 rows with zero-shot CoT, Self Correction, Multi-Agent Debate and Multi-Agent Peer Review. New multimodal comparisons evaluate CLIPScore, ImageReward, PickScore and, on AGIQA only, X-IQE. G-Eval and Analyze-Rate remain NLG comparators, while the fine-tuning comparison drops its GPT-3.5 reference row.

E3.justification: SummEval evaluation expands from 200 selected samples to the full 1,600. The main peer models change from GPT-3.5, Gemini-Pro and Mixtral to Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-Nemo-12B and Gemma-2-9B, with GPT-4o-mini replacing the GPT-3.5 chair. New multimodal protocols use two VLM peers, a GPT-4o chair, 864 usable ICQD samples and 500 AGIQA samples selected for rating coverage. Cost, timing and threshold-based error evaluations are also introduced.

E4.justification: V2 adds peer-count/composition and weaker-chair ablations, aggregate peer/chair error analysis, ProTeGi optimization comparisons, score-versus-comment communication tests, SummEval distribution analysis and inference timing. V1's critic-strategy experiments, incremental component ablation and worked evaluation, fine-tuning and reasoning case studies disappear. Prompt ablations are substantially redesigned around TopicalChat.

E5.justification: V1 specifies two-run averaging for its prompt ablation but provides no uncertainty estimates or significance tests. V2 reports three-run averages for NLG and reasoning, adds ± values to reasoning Table 4, and reports paired t-test p-values in Appendix M. These are substantial reporting additions; the ± statistic is not clearly defined, and the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs for otherwise identical experiments.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. TopicalChat average Spearman correlation changes from 0.597 in v1 Table 2 to 0.628 for Turbo and 0.579 for Lite in v2 Table 2 under changed models and protocols, not a matched-setting improvement. V2 adds multimodal results, including Turbo correlations of 0.497 on ICQD and 0.657 on AGIQA, and revises reasoning and TopicalChat fine-tuning results. StrategyQA, SummEval fine-tuning and critic-strategy results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 Equations 1–4 and Algorithm 1 express the peer/chair evaluations, multiple responses and score averaging already described procedurally in v1 Section 2 and Appendix A. This adds notation and pseudocode, without new substantive mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from NLG evaluation, instruction tuning and three reasoning benchmarks to a tuning-free hierarchy for text/image evaluation and four reasoning benchmarks. Turbo/Lite and approximately 7.7-fold efficiency become headline claims. Fine-tuning remains in an appendix but loses its central contribution status, and the earlier specific SummEval and GPT-3.5/GPT-4 improvement claims are replaced.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for task-dependent differences between hierarchy and debate, guidance on peer count and chair strength, and interpretations of chair dependence on correct peers. Appendix G newly argues that SummEval's skewed ratings undermine its suitability. Limitations shift toward computational cost, weaker chairs, missing inter-peer discussion and untested modalities, while several configuration questions left open in v1 receive empirical discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds API-provider information, task-specific generation limits, an AutoPrompt worked example, expanded task prompts and repository/PyPI links claiming public access. V1 only promised code after review. Conversely, v1's explicit fine-tuning split details and A100 hardware statement disappear. V2 also retains a future-release statement in Section 11, leaving its availability wording inconsistent.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially into multimodal quality assessment, with CLIPScore, ImageReward, PickScore, HyperIQA and X-IQE, and into prompt optimization through OPRO, APE and ProTeGi. ReConCile changes from a central empirical comparator to an explicitly excluded baseline because of architectural differences in Appendix I. The positioning increasingly emphasizes hierarchy and efficiency relative to debate-based systems.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and the main narrative is reorganized into methodology, experiments, results and analysis. SummEval results and fine-tuning move to appendices; limitations and related work are rewritten; prompts are reorganized by task. A reproducibility statement replaces the former potential-risks section.

P2.justification: V2 changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR format and redraws the framework illustration around the hierarchy and Turbo/Lite variants. It adds a multimodal diagram and peer-scaling, error-analysis, rating-distribution and timing plots. Tables gain variant, cost and uncertainty structure. The critic diagram disappears, while v1 Figure 2's prompting schema is retained as v2 Figure 4.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses validation gaps: multimodal applicability is tested rather than merely proposed, SummEval uses the full test set, and peer-count, chair-strength and error analyses investigate configuration limits explicitly left open in v1. Broader reasoning comparisons and repeated-run reporting further strengthen assessment. These gains outweigh reduced fine-tuning documentation and remaining overclaims: notably, the claim that both variants beat NLG baselines is too broad, since Lite's SummEval average Spearman correlation is 0.447 versus G-Eval's 0.472 in Table 9.
